judgments.rationale:
[visual context] This is the 'Ver programa' link of slide 5, to /educativo/programas/acesseparaperceber (Acesse para Perceber). The page has 7 'Ver programa' links, one per slide of the #programs-carousel Swiper (arteparamaiores, monnaescola, euparticipo, primeirospassos, acesseparaperceber, monparatodos, feriasnomon). Looking for a way out: none has a title, aria-label or aria-describedby; the link is a sibling of the description

, not inside it, and not in a list item or table cell; the program name is shown only by a logo (programa_educativo_site_N.svg) with no alt; the slides carry no aria-hidden or inert, so all 7 are in the tree and focusable. The nearest heading before every one of the 7 is the same schedule-card h5 ('Arte para Maiores | Daquilo que nos escapa | Encontro online'), so their counted contexts are identical and they form one R1 set. The 7 destinations are different programs (packet headings differ), not equivalent resources, and visual information tells them apart (each slide shows its program logo, e.g. 'MON. Arte para Maiores', a photo and a description). By R1 every link of the set fails 2.4.4, and the claim (shared text, 7 places, nothing around it tells it apart) names that failure and is true of the capture. The nested inside the is in the server HTML too; the snapshot is the client-rendered DOM a browser with scripts ends with. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 has the same 7 links, hrefs, logo images without alt and markup, so the capture does not differ.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter e-mail input's placeholder 'Seu e-mail', 18px weight 400 (not large text, so 4.5:1 applies). Reasons it could pass that I checked: a stricter-than-WCAG reading (no: Understanding 1.4.3 says the criterion 'applies to text in the page, including placeholder text'); an exception (the field is active, the text is not decorative or a logo, and it is the field's only visible label); a wrong colour reading (no: the screenshot's glyph pixels are #a0aec0 at darkest on #ffffff, 2.26:1, and the live CSS sets ::placeholder to var(--chakra-colors-gray-400) = #A0AEC0 with no override on css-1k89cub, background inherited from the white form panel). The live page fetched on 2026-11-21 has the same input and styles, so the capture does not differ. The claim states the measured failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: A text input with placeholder 'Seu nome completo' ('your full name') in the 'Receba notícias' newsletter form: it collects the user's own full name, the 'name' input purpose, and HTML supports autocomplete. The snapshot HTML and the live server HTML (fetched 2026-11-21, no 'autocomplete' anywhere in the page) show no autocomplete attribute and no other mechanism that identifies the purpose, so the purpose cannot be programmatically determined (H98 not met). I found no reason to clear it: the field is not about a third party and is not a free-text field outside the list. The claim names exactly this.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter form's input type=email with placeholder 'Seu e-mail' ('your e-mail') collects the user's own e-mail address, the 'email' input purpose. The only possible escape is type=email, but that states a data format, not that the value is the user's own address, and it is not a 1.3.5 technique; there is no autocomplete attribute in the snapshot or in the live HTML (fetched 2026-11-21). So the field fails 1.3.5, as the claim says.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: No claim. The exhibitions-carousel card link to /exposicoes/o-verso-da-pagina-contem-o-outro-lado has the accessible name 'Até 28 de março de 2027 O verso da página contém o outro lado', which holds the exhibition's title (an h3 inside the link), and the destination is that exhibition's page, so its purpose is clear from the link text alone. No other link on the page shares that name with a different destination. The photo inside lacks alt (a 1.1.1 matter, not 2.4.4). The live HTML has the same link and markup. It meets 2.4.4, so Rampa was right not to report it.
